changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 1 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/7546-chart-series-keys-declared.md`

- names `AdvancedChartImpl.tsx` → `packages/plugin-charts/src/AdvancedChartImpl.tsx` — edited by this change

  > Every one of the six is read by `normalizeSeries` (`@object-ui/plugin-charts`, `normalizeChartSchema.ts:242-255`) and does real work in `AdvancedChartImpl.tsx` — `label` names the legend entry, `variant === 'comparison'` selects the muted overlay, `opacity` / `dashArray` set stroke and fill, `stack` becomes Recharts' `stackId`, `yAxis` binds the secondary axis. Any consumer of the parse output — `objectui check` / `objectui validate` via `safeValidateSchema`, a JSON schema derived from the mirror, or any pipeline that keeps `parse()`'s result — lost them outright.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `bf14b6460` (merge-base with origin/main): 4 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1586 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (2174 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36325658994)

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `423704076be539be7a42220d8e3060e1ebc97c05`

### ① Derived judgments

**The predicate is correct.** `hasNoCarriedSeriesKey` (`AdvancedChartImpl.tsx`) returns the keys only when every deduplicated `dataKey` meets three conditions: it is a string, it matches `/^[^.[]+$/`, and for every row it fails `row != null && typeof row === 'object' && key in row`. That is exactly "no row has the key", and it is the same test `hasNoCategoryKey` uses.
- **A key present with the value `undefined` or `null`:** `in` reports it as present, so it is carried and passes to `no-numeric-value`. This is pinned: all-`null` rows give `no-numeric-value`.
- **Path-shaped keys:** a key containing `.` or `[` is never judged absent. This is pinned: `a.b` draws, and an unresolved `a.b` stays silent.
- **Non-string or empty keys:** never judged absent.
- **Prototype names such as `toString`:** `in` counts them as carried, while `no-numeric-value`'s `hasOwnProperty` gate treats them as unresolved. The tile stays silent, which errs toward silence and matches the category guard. Not a defect.
- **Empty data set (0 rows):** no regression. The guard returns `null` when `rows.length === 0`, as its three siblings do, and the query-backed empty state is decided upstream at `ObjectChart.tsx:1446`, before this component is reached. Advisory: no test pins the 0-row case for the new guard.

**Precedence is sound.** The order is `missing-category-key`, then `no-plottable-series`, then `missing-series-key`, then `no-numeric-value`, both in how the guards are gated and in the order of the early returns.
- **`hasNoNumericSeriesValue` body:** byte-identical against main. Only its doc paragraph changed.
- **The added gate `|| missingSeriesKeys`:** it changes nothing, because the two predicates cannot both fire. The new guard needs every key to fail `in`. `no-numeric-value` stays `null` unless every key is some row's own property. So objectui#7195's judgment scope does not move, as the triage's point 3 requires.
- **Hooks:** the new `useEffect` sits before every early return in the wrapper, which keeps the hook list fixed. Its dependencies are two JSON strings.
- **The warning:** the dev's claim says the tile "emits the category refusal's console warning". It actually emits its own warning built the same way: the missing keys plus the FIRST row's keys, which is also what the category warning prints. The changeset's "the keys the rows do carry" is qualified by "as the category refusal's warning does". Acceptable.

**The two re-decided pins meet the triage.**
- **`countSeriesKeyRender-8266`:** new header section "Re-decided on purpose by objectui#10396 — the zero arm now REFUSES". The `value` arm now asserts 0 marks, 0 series, `missing-series-key`, "no row has a value field", ticks `[]` and no empty state. The harness gains only `refusalText`. The `count` arm and the setup are unchanged.
- **`categoryAxisKeyRender-8269`:** new header section "Re-decided on purpose by objectui#10396 — the FIRST row now refuses". The baseline table is kept as history. Only `status/value` is rewritten. `name/value` and `name/count` gain a comment only, which turns them into the precedence pin.
- Neither file is deleted, and no other assertion changes.

**Text and i18n are consistent with the nearest siblings, but one code comment is wrong.** The new sentence is an English JSX literal, like `missing-category-key` (the sibling it mirrors), both `no-plottable-series` sentences, `no-numeric-value`, `no-positive-magnitude`, `no-plottable-points` and `no-positive-flow`. One sibling IS translated: `scatter-multi-series` goes through `tt('chart.scatterOneMeasure', …)` in `SeriesArityRefusal`, and the key is in all ten packs.
- The `MissingSeriesKeyRefusal` doc comment says "English literal, no locale key, matching every sibling sentence". That is false.
- Replacement (non-blocking): "English literal, no locale key, like `missing-category-key`, `no-plottable-series` and `no-numeric-value`; of this file's refusals only `scatter-multi-series` resolves through a locale key (`chart.scatterOneMeasure`)."
- The PR body's H3 names only the four literal siblings. Each of its sentences is true, but it leaves out the one sibling that is translated.

**The dead-key partial case is worded accurately, but the ruling is not on record.** The Acceptance note says an absent key beside an all-boolean key draws nothing, silently, as on base, and that neither refusal fires. That matches the code and the pin, which asserts no refusal and 0 marks, and it correctly ties the `no-numeric-value` half to the triage's point 3 ("do not change #7195's judgment scope"). However, no seat ruling is recorded anywhere I can read:
- The card has only the four named comments.
- The dev report still lists this as `open_questions` with recommendation A.
- The PR does not cite a ruling.

The seat should post its ruling on the card so that open question is closed on the record.

**The 7195 dated note is in the objectui#10533 form.** It matches `.changeset/10156-edit-form-writes-only-changed-fields.md:25`: "⚠️ **Dated note, 2026-09-27 — … — objectui#10396.** Later in this same release … The rest of this entry is kept as the reading of this change; the objectui#10396 entry states …".
- It is appended at the end of the entry. The frontmatter md5 is equal at base and head.
- It is true: a dotted path, or an absent key beside a carried key, keeps both refusals silent.

**The pins are real and not tautological.** They render the real component or chain and read the DOM (mark counts, `data-chart-error`, text), with a lit control for every family. The counts are consistent: new file 46 tests, the 8266 pin 3, the 8269 pin 8, total 57. The 16 claimed red on base are exactly the refusal assertions: 6 family refusals, every-key-absent, the warning, 6 "whatever else it declares" cases, the 8266 `value` arm and the 8269 `status/value` case. Ablating `hasNoCarriedSeriesKey(props)` to `null` would redden the same 16.

Non-blocking prose left false:
- `AdvancedChartImpl.noNumericValue.test.tsx:543-545` is outside the claimed surface and was knowingly left, with no carrier. Its title reads "left to its own question" and its comment reads "whose render pins keep it silent until it is re-decided on its own". Both are now false; the assertion is still true.
- Replacement for the comment: "A different diagnosis, the binding names a column the rows do not have; since objectui#10396 it gets its own `missing-series-key`, never this code." Suggested title: "a bound key NO row carries is not this code (objectui#10396 owns it)".

### ② Semver level

`patch` is correct.
- It is a bug fix under the objectui `.changeset/README.md` levels, and it follows the precedent of the `no-numeric-value` refusal (objectui#7195), which also shipped as `patch`.
- No export or type moves. The diff adds no `export` line; `hasNoCarriedSeriesKey` and `MissingSeriesKeyRefusal` are module-private; `AdvancedChartImplProps` is untouched. Clause-② no is correct.

The changeset, read sentence by sentence, is true against the code.
- "Cartesian" in its first sentence is bounded by the closing sentence, which says scatter never receives this code.
- "Dotted key" is narrower than the code, which also exempts keys containing `[`. Acceptable.

The PR body, read sentence by sentence, is true, apart from the H3 omission noted in ①.

Advisory: `.changeset/8266-dashboard-count-aggregate-series-key.md:19-20` says "neither of the renderer's two guards fires on it". That stays literally true of the two guards it names, but its implication that nothing says so is false after this change in the same release. The claims gate did not flag it because it matches file names only. An optional dated note in the objectui#10533 form would close it.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **CI on the head:** 43 check runs, all completed: 40 `success` and 3 `skipped` (`dependabot`, `Test (coverage)`, `Test (coverage shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/4)`). All eight Test shards, Lint, Type Check, Build & E2E, Test (dist pins), the changeset gates, Spec Main Shape Gate and Governed Surface Queue Guard are `success`. The combined status (Vercel) is `success`.
- **`git merge-tree --write-tree` against current main `bf14b6460`:** exit 0, clean. Main has not touched `packages/plugin-charts` or the 7195 changeset since base `17cc3a377`.
- **Open PRs touching these files:** none. I read the file lists of all 10 other open PRs, including every page of release PR objectui#5400 (1732 files). objectui#8941 touches `plugin-charts/package.json` only; objectui#5400 touches `plugin-charts` `CHANGELOG.md` and `package.json` only.
- **Governed predicate:** `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr objectstack-ai/objectui#10787` reports 0 of 6 paths governed (NOT governed). The size is 450 changed lines, under the human-merge threshold.
- **Draft state:** the PR is still a draft and must be marked ready before it can land. Assignee is `os-elon-musk`. Mergeable state is `clean`.
